_note: Causilo exported at the released architecture, weight-free (opset 18). (x, y)-only: y carries ONLY the training targets, so its length S IS train_size; no cat_mask / d input. The graph normalises its own features (train-prefix z-score, two-stage 4-sigma bounds, arcsinh tails) and, for regression, standardises the target and inverts the scaler, so the engine feeds RAW targets and features and reads the output directly. Output [1,T,C]: every row is a prediction; rows < S are in-context fitted values (the context presented a second time as queries -- the cheap alternative measured fitted R2 0.50 on a clean linear problem where query R2 was 0.999). C = 10 for classification; for regression C = 1, the mean over the 999 output channels. Verified against upstream CausiloClassifier/CausiloRegressor with n_estimators=1 on real weights: probabilities within 1e-5, identical labels. The leaderboard figure is an 8-member ensemble, which the engine does not run.
